name: Prepare Board and committee meeting packages
summary: The board secretariat prepares the papers for each meeting of the Board of Directors and its five standing committees, about 36 regular and 18 special meetings in fiscal 2022. The corporate secretary sets the agenda with the chair and CEO, a specialist calls for papers from Finance, Risk, Total Fund Management, Talent, Legal, Compliance and Internal Audit, the accountable executives sign off their papers, and the CEO and chair preview the pack before it is published on the board portal about a week before the meeting. After the meeting the secretariat drafts minutes, gets them reviewed and circulates the action log. Late papers, several layers of executive sign-off and long packs make the cycle slow, and most elapsed time is owners drafting and waiting for the meeting date.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national pension fund investment manager with about 2,050 employees, an independent Board of 11 to 12 directors and five standing committees, governed by a federal statute.
baseline.notes: Snapshot of fiscal 2022 when all meetings were held by videoconference. Paper drafting by owners belongs to the upstream processes; this workflow counts only the secretariat's work and executive sign-off.

trigger: A meeting on the annual Board calendar comes due (or a special meeting is called) and the papers it needs are being produced by the reporting processes.
end_state: The package was published to directors, the meeting was held, the chair-approved draft minutes and action log were circulated and the record was filed; formal minute approval happens at the next meeting.

volume.seasonality: Heavier in May to June (annual results, audited statements, compensation) and February to March (business plan, budget, risk appetite); special meetings cluster around large transactions.

evidence.note: Regular meetings: 27 in F2020, 42 in F2021 and 36 in F2022 (2.3 to 3.5 a month); with special meetings up to 54 in F2022 (4.5 a month).
Runs the secretariat under the General Counsel and Corporate Secretary (F2022). FTE is the author's estimate from about 15 hours per meeting at three meetings a month plus planning outside cases.

Company secretary staff prepare and distribute packs and minutes. FTE is the author's estimate from about 40 hours per meeting; the rest of the six-person team's time goes to Board approval items, director onboarding, evaluations and subsidiary governance.

roles.title: President and Chief Executive Officer
roles.department: Office of the President and CEO

evidence.note: The CEO helps build the agenda and clears the pack. FTE from about 1.5 hours per meeting.

roles.title: Senior Managing Director and Chief Financial and Risk Officer

evidence.note: The CFRO meets the Audit and Risk Committees and owns finance and risk papers (F2022). FTE from about 1.5 hours per routed meeting.

roles.title: Senior Managing Director and Chief Investment Officer

evidence.note: The CIO owns portfolio, performance and pipeline papers for the ISC and Board. FTE from about 2 hours per routed meeting.

roles.title: Senior Managing Director, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary
roles.department: General Counsel's office and legal operations

evidence.note: The General Counsel is Corporate Secretary and reviews resolutions and sensitive minutes. FTE from hands-on time per meeting.

roles.title: Senior Managing Director and Chief Talent Officer

evidence.note: The Chief Talent Officer owns HRCC papers. FTE from about 2 hours per HRCC meeting, five to nine a year.
The Head of Risk owns risk reports to the Risk Committee. FTE from hands-on time per Risk Committee meeting.

roles.title: Managing Director, Head of Assurance and Advisory

The Chief Compliance Officer owns compliance reports for the Audit and Governance Committees. FTE from hands-on time per meeting.

systems.name: Document management and investment committee memo repository

steps.name: Draft agenda from the annual timetable
steps.description: The Managing Director, Associate Corporate Secretary opens the committee's annual timetable and the action log from the last meeting, lists the standing items due (quarterly reports, policy reviews, approvals) and adds items management has flagged, then drafts the agenda with time slots and paper owners.

error.defect_description: A standing item due under the terms of reference is left off the agenda.

evidence.note: The ISC terms of reference include a timetable of items by meeting; agenda first, then deadlines. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Agree agenda with chair and CEO
steps.description: The corporate secretary walks the committee chair and the CEO through the draft agenda by call, adjusts items, order and time allocations, and records the chair's approval of the final agenda and the list of papers required.

error.defect_description: Chair and CEO priorities are recorded inconsistently, so a paper is commissioned with the wrong scope.

control.basis: Board and committee guidelines: the chair approves the agenda

evidence.note: The CEO and chair build the agenda and the chair approves it. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Issue call for papers
steps.description: A board secretariat specialist emails each paper owner the approved agenda item, the paper template with its cover sheet (purpose, decision sought, key points), the page guideline and the submission deadline, and sets up the meeting folder on the board portal.

error.defect_description: A deadline or template is sent to the wrong owner or omitted.

evidence.note: Set submission deadlines for executives and committees and use templates. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Track submissions and chase late papers
steps.description: While owners in Finance, Risk, Total Fund Management, Talent, Legal and Internal Audit draft their papers, the specialist keeps a tracker of each paper's status, sends reminders before and after the deadline and escalates missing papers to the corporate secretary.

error.defect_description: None introduced; late papers compress review time downstream.

evidence.note: Late contributions hold up the whole pack. The 1.5 to 2.5 weeks of drafting time before the deadline is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Chase revised papers
steps.description: When a paper is returned, the specialist logs the reason in the tracker, agrees a resubmission date with the owner, follows up until the revised paper arrives and sends it back through the completeness check and executive sign-off.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of the turnaround for a returned board paper.

steps.name: Check papers for completeness and format
steps.description: The specialist opens each paper, checks the cover sheet, page length, numbering and cross-references, confirms figures match the source report named, and returns papers that miss the template or the decision request before routing the rest to the accountable executive by meeting type.

error.defect_description: A figure that disagrees between two papers is not noticed.

next.condition: papers returned to owners for rework
Board or Audit Committee meeting: finance papers to the CFRO
Risk Committee meeting: risk report to the Head of Risk
Investment Strategy Committee meeting: investment papers to the CIO
Human Resources and Compensation Committee meeting

evidence.note: Collect and check documents for accuracy and completeness before compiling. Routing shares follow the F2022 meeting mix (Board and ISC 8 each, other committees 5 each, plus specials).

steps.name: CFRO signs off finance and risk papers
steps.description: The Chief Financial and Risk Officer reads the financial statements, business plan, performance and expense papers for the meeting, asks owners for changes by email and confirms the papers can go to the directors.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Board expectations of management: timely disclosure of all material information; executive accountability for papers

next.condition: Board meeting: investment papers to the CIO next
Audit Committee meeting: internal audit report next

evidence.note: The Audit and Risk Committees meet separately with the CFRO; management must disclose material information to the Board. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Head of Risk reviews the risk report
steps.description: The Managing Director, Head of Risk reads the quarterly risk report, limit usage, breach summaries and stress test results, checks the narrative explains the movements and agrees any changes with the risk team before passing it to the CFRO.

error.defect_description: A limit status in the narrative disagrees with the dashboard.

control.basis: Investment Statement s. 9.10: total risk exposures reported to the Board at least quarterly

evidence.note: The Risk Committee monitors the risk profile against risk appetite and receives risk and stress results. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: CIO signs off portfolio and investment papers
steps.description: The Chief Investment Officer reads the portfolio performance, pipeline, portfolio design and transaction papers, checks that messages are consistent across departments and the performance report, and approves them or sends comments back to the owners.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: ISC terms of reference: quarterly reports on portfolio performance and pipelines; CIO accountability

evidence.note: The ISC receives quarterly reports on performance and pipelines; the Board receives quarterly portfolio reports. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Head of internal audit clears the audit report
steps.description: The Managing Director, Head of Assurance and Advisory reviews the internal audit status report, open findings and plan changes for the Audit Committee and confirms the content independently of management.

error.defect_description: An overdue finding is shown as closed.

control.basis: Audit Committee oversight of internal audit; internal audit reports functionally to the Audit Committee chair

evidence.note: The Audit Committee oversees internal audit and meets the auditors without management. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Chief Compliance Officer clears the compliance report
steps.description: The Chief Compliance Officer reviews the compliance report on Code of Conduct attestations, breaches and regulatory matters, checks names and cases are presented appropriately and approves it for the pack.

error.defect_description: A personal case is described in more detail than the committee needs.

control.basis: Governance Committee oversight of the Code of Conduct

evidence.note: The Governance Committee reviews and monitors the application of the Code of Conduct. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Chief Talent Officer signs off compensation papers
steps.description: The Chief Talent Officer reviews the HRCC papers on incentive outcomes, compensation framework, succession and organisation changes, checks figures with Total Rewards and approves them.

error.defect_description: An incentive figure is out of date against the final performance numbers.

control.basis: HRCC mandate: committee reviews compensation framework and succession

evidence.note: The HRCC administers executive evaluation and reviews the compensation framework. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: General Counsel reviews governance items and resolutions
steps.description: The General Counsel and Corporate Secretary reviews draft resolutions, governance policy changes and any matter needing legal privilege, checks wording against the Act and by-laws, and returns comments to the secretariat.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: the fund's governing act and by-laws: form of Board resolutions and conflict disclosure

next.condition: Governance Committee meeting: compliance report next

evidence.note: Resolutions and conflict rules are set in the Act; the General Counsel is Corporate Secretary. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Corporate secretary reviews the draft pack
steps.description: The corporate secretary reads the assembled papers against the agenda, checks the decision requested in each cover sheet, removes duplication and sends papers back to owners when a paper is unclear, too long or inconsistent with another.

error.defect_description: Two papers present different versions of the same figure.

control.basis: Corporate Secretary accountability for Board materials

next.condition: paper returned to its owner for rewrite

evidence.note: Review and approve the pack in a tracked workflow before distribution. Rework share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: CEO clears the pack
steps.description: The President and CEO reads the cover memo and key papers, asks for changes to messages or emphasis and confirms the pack can go to the chair.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Board expectations of management: CEO accountable for material disclosed to the Board

evidence.note: The preparer works with the CEO and CFO; the CEO builds the agenda with the chair. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Chair previews the pack
steps.description: The committee chair, an independent director outside the organisation, reviews the near-final pack on the portal, sometimes after a short call with the corporate secretary, and asks for any last changes.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Chairs approve agendas and preparers work with committee chairs. Wait is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Compile and publish the pack on the board portal
steps.description: The specialist merges the final papers into the meeting book, adds the agenda, previous minutes and action log, bookmarks and paginates a pack that often runs to a few hundred pages, sets reader permissions and publishes it with a notice to directors.

error.defect_description: A superseded version of a paper or a wrong page order is published.

control.basis: Information security: board portal access limited to named directors and officers

evidence.note: Distribute through a board portal; average pack 226 pages; aim for 7 to 10 days before the meeting. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Post late and corrected papers
steps.description: When an owner misses the pack deadline or a figure changes, the specialist loads the supplementary paper or corrected page, flags it in the portal and notifies directors of the change.

error.defect_description: Directors read the superseded version.

evidence.note: Late contributions are a common problem; portals notify directors of updates. Share of meetings with late papers is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Directors read the pack before the meeting
steps.description: Directors, who are outside the organisation, read the pack on the portal in the days before the meeting; the elapsed time is set by how far ahead of the meeting the pack was published.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Packs are meant to reach directors 7 to 10 days ahead; 55% of directors receive them fewer than five days ahead. The mode of 7 days is the author's reading of these figures.

steps.name: Relay directors' advance questions
steps.description: The specialist collects questions sent by directors, forwards each to the paper owner, gathers short written answers or adds the topic to the presenter's briefing, and posts responses to the portal before the meeting.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for directors who read packs in advance.

steps.name: Run the meeting and record proceedings
steps.description: The corporate secretary attends the videoconference meeting as secretary, confirms quorum, records decisions, dissents and declared conflicts, keeps notes of discussion and actions, and leaves for the sessions held without management.

error.defect_description: A decision condition or action owner is not captured in the notes.

control.basis: the fund's governing act ss. 21 and 22: dissent and conflicts of interest entered in the minutes

evidence.note: F2022 meetings were held by videoconference with sessions without management at every regular meeting; dissent and conflicts must be minuted. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Draft minutes and the action log
steps.description: A specialist writes the draft minutes from the secretary's notes and recording of decisions, words each resolution as passed, and updates the action log with owners and due dates.

error.defect_description: A resolution is worded differently from what was passed, or an action is missed.

control.basis: the fund's governing act s. 19(2): written resolutions kept with the minutes; corporate records

evidence.note: Minutes record decisions and actions with dates; the Act requires certain matters in the minutes. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Corporate secretary reviews draft minutes
steps.description: The corporate secretary compares the draft minutes with the meeting notes and resolutions, tightens wording on sensitive matters and decides whether the General Counsel needs to see them.

error.defect_description: A wording issue on a privileged matter is missed.

next.condition: conflict, dissent, privileged or contentious matter

evidence.note: Author's estimate; a second review is common for minutes of a statutory body.

steps.name: General Counsel reviews sensitive minutes
steps.description: The General Counsel reads minutes that record conflicts, dissents, written resolutions or privileged legal advice and confirms the record meets the Act and protects privilege.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: the fund's governing act ss. 19 to 22: resolutions, dissent and conflicts recorded in the minutes

evidence.note: The Act specifies matters that must be minuted. Share and times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Committee chair reviews draft minutes
steps.description: The draft minutes go to the committee chair, who reads them on the portal and returns comments or approval for circulation; formal approval follows at the next meeting.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Draft minutes go to the chair within two to three working days and to all directors within a week. The longer wait here reflects a larger review chain and is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Circulate minutes and action log to owners
steps.description: The specialist posts the chair-approved draft minutes for directors, sends each action owner their items with due dates and updates the tracker that feeds the next meeting's agenda.

error.defect_description: An action is sent to the wrong owner.

evidence.note: Minutes and actions with completion dates go to all directors. Times are the author's estimates.

steps.name: File the record and report to the Board
steps.description: The specialist files the pack, minutes and signed resolutions in the document store, and for committee meetings adds the minutes to the next Board pack so the committee chair can report orally, as the terms of reference require.

error.defect_description: A signed resolution is filed without its supporting paper.

control.basis: ISC terms of reference s. 6.0: committee reports to the Board by distributing minutes and an oral report

evidence.note: Committees report by distributing minutes and an oral report at the next Board meeting. Times are the author's estimates.

exceptions.name: Paper rewritten after secretariat or corporate secretary review
exceptions.description: A paper misses the template, runs too long or conflicts with another paper and goes back to its owner, who revises it and gets executive sign-off again.

exceptions.name: CEO or chair asks for changes
exceptions.description: The CEO or the committee chair asks for a different emphasis or extra information, so the corporate secretary works the change through the owner before publication.

exceptions.name: Late or corrected papers after publication
exceptions.description: An owner misses the pack deadline (for example quarter-end figures not final) or finds an error, and a supplementary paper is posted a few days before the meeting.

exceptions.name: Special meeting at short notice
exceptions.description: A special meeting for a time-critical approval runs the same steps compressed into a few days with a short pack; Board transaction approvals are handled in the separate Board investment approval process.

exceptions.name: Minutes edited after chair review
exceptions.description: The chair asks for wording changes and the minutes cycle through drafting and review again.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from drafting the agenda to filing the chair-approved minutes
benchmarks.population: Board and committee meetings of a large Canadian pension investment manager

evidence.note: Author's estimate built from documented stages: agenda and call for papers four to six weeks ahead, pack distributed 7 to 10 days ahead, draft minutes to the chair within days and to directors within a week, with longer review chains assumed for a large statutory body.
Eight Board, five Audit, five HRCC, five Governance, five Risk and eight ISC regular meetings.
Attendance table maxima: 14 Board, 12 ISC, 6 Audit, 7 Governance, 9 HRCC, 6 Risk.
Section 4.0.

benchmarks.population: Board Intelligence client and survey base

evidence.note: Up 30% since 2019; only 40% of packs under 100 pages.
10 to 14 days for complex meetings.

pain_points.description: Papers arrive late from owners who are also closing the quarter, compressing secretariat and executive review into a few days and forcing supplementary papers after the pack is published.

evidence.note: Late contributions hold up packs; 55% of directors get packs fewer than five days ahead.

pain_points.description: Several layers of sign-off (owner, executive, corporate secretary, CEO, chair) add days of waiting for busy approvers and can send a paper back to the start.

evidence.note: Author's reading of the sign-off chain described for this organisation.

pain_points.description: Packs run to hundreds of pages, so checking consistency of figures across papers is slow and errors slip through to corrections.

evidence.note: Average pack 226 pages.

pain_points.description: Minutes take one to three weeks to reach directors because they pass through the corporate secretary, sometimes the General Counsel, and the chair.

evidence.note: Guidance is a week; the longer chain here is the author's estimate.

Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

sources.title: Terms of Reference for the Investment Strategy Committee (June 22, 2022)
sources.supports: The committee is the full Board and meets at least four times a year; annual timetable of agenda items by meeting (Mar/Apr, May, June, Sep, Nov, Feb); quarterly reports on performance and pipelines; it reports to the Board by distributing its minutes and an oral report at the next Board meeting. Read from a text copy saved under scratch/.

sources.title: the fund's governing act (S.C. 1997, c. 40), sections 11 to 22
sources.publisher: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
sources.supports: Written resolutions signed by all directors are valid and kept with the minutes (s. 19); directors may take part by telephone or other facilities (s. 20); a director's dissent must be entered in the minutes or sent in writing (s. 21); conflicts of interest must be disclosed and entered in the minutes (s. 22).

sources.title: A guide to creating effective board packs
sources.supports: Average board pack 226 pages, up 30% since 2019, with only 40% under 100 pages; papers should be no longer than five pages; packs ideally reach directors at least a week ahead but 55% of directors receive them fewer than five days before; set submission deadlines early, review in a tracked workflow and distribute through a board portal.

sources.title: Top tips for managing the board meeting cycle
sources.supports: The CEO and chair build the agenda and the chair approves it; the pack should reach directors the week before; draft minutes go to the chair within two to three working days and to all directors within a week; actions carry completion dates; approvals between meetings are ratified at the next meeting.

sources.title: Board pack: guide and best practices
sources.supports: Steps: define objectives, prepare the agenda, set submission deadlines for executives and committees, collect and check documents, organise by priority, distribute at least 7 to 10 days before the meeting (10 to 14 days for complex meetings); late contributions hold up the whole pack; the preparer is usually the company secretary working with the CEO, CFO and committee chairs; packs typically 30 to 100 pages.

assumptions: The unit of work mixes regular Board and committee meetings; routing shares at s05 follow the F2022 regular meeting mix (Board and ISC eight each, other committees five each) and lean toward the Board and ISC because most special meetings were Board or ISC meetings.
Paper drafting by owners (risk, performance, financial statements, business plan, audit and compliance reports) is counted in the upstream processes; here it appears only as the wait at s04.
Board directors are outside parties, so the chair's preview (s14), directors' reading (s17) and the chair's minute review (s23) are external waits with no labour cost.
The process map gives no trigger for HRCC papers (the compensation cycle does not produce to this process); HRCC meetings are covered by the routing at s05 and the CTO sign-off at s10.
Trigger shares are the author's mapping of which upstream report anchors each kind of meeting; in practice the annual calendar starts each case.
The secretariat's internal approval thresholds, pack deadlines and minute turnaround targets are not published; times are estimates anchored on practitioner guidance.
Loaded costs are taken from the organisation file (total compensation including incentive pay times 1.25 overhead over 1,950 paid hours).
The simulated median runs about 10% above the benchmark estimate because paper rework, CEO and chair changes and minute edits loop back through review steps in about 45% of meetings.
